utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-96-23/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could I have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and I appear here with case manager Verica Balikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Tjarda Van der Spoel, duty counsel for Mr. Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that Mr. Zelenovic is present as well. There seems to be a technical problem. Do you hear me in a language you understand, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you missed my first words. I asked the registrar to call the case, and then I asked the parties to present themselves; Madam Uertz-Retzlaff for the Prosecution, Mr. Tjarda Van der Spoel as duty counsel. You may be seated, Mr. Zelenovic. Mr. Zelenovic, we are here this morning to invite you to enter a plea -- you may be seated. You don't have to stand all the time. To invite you to enter a plea. You made your initial appearance on the 13th of June, and you then have chosen to delay entering a plea. According to the Rules, you're allowed to do so for 30 days. Therefore, we'll proceed. First of all, Mr. Zelenovic, you are still represented or assisted by duty counsel, Mr. Van der Spoel. I know that you wanted to be represented by another lawyer. I also do understand that that would be Mr. Ognjanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, did you have an opportunity to speak with Mr. Ognjanovic until now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you discuss with him the indictment that is brought against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore you then would not have discussed either whether you want to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty, or did you have an opportunity to speak with him about that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I spoke to him on the phone yesterday. He is supposed to arrive at noon today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We had scheduling problems to the extent that this hearing was scheduled. From what I do understand, Mr. Ognjanovic did not fully yet qualify to be assigned as counsel. Let me ask Mr. Van der Spoel whether he has had any communication with Mr. Ognjanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I have not. I was quite worried about the lack of assignment of Defence counsel to Mr. Zelenovic. That's why I've communicated quite often with OLAD and visited Mr. Zelenovic last week, Friday, to discuss his position again, also if he wanted to discuss the indictment or other things that could be of importance. He said: No, I am waiting for my fully assigned counsel. Then again I phoned OLAD on Friday and then they told me that yesterday there should be a kind of language course or examination. I was informed yesterday afternoon that that did not happen, and that next week again there will be another chance for the fully assigned counsel perhaps to pass that examination. And that's the situation as I see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zelenovic, please be seated. It's not necessary to stand all the time. Did you read the indictment in a version -- in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you understand what the charges against you are?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Upon the basis of your telephone conversation you said you had yesterday with Mr. Ognjanovic, do you feel that you are in a position to enter a plea, that is to tell me whether you consider yourself to be guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's supposed to arrive at noon, and we are supposed to meet at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zelenovic, but --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And he told me: If you have to enter a plea, enter a plea of not guilty, if you have to. However, I would like to see him first. He did instruct me to plead not guilty if I am asked to enter a plea before I meet with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest to the parties -- I'm informing the parties that I'm considering not to hear any plea today under the present circumstances. It would be -- well, let's call of it a kind of an emergency not guilty plea, which doesn't make much sense under the present circumstances. At the same time, I'm very concerned about the loss of time because if you have no plea this could delay further working on the case, both for Prosecution and Defence. I also keep in mind that we're about to start a recess, which might cause a situation in which no substantial progress will be made anyhow. So I'd like to hear from you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, and from you, Mr. Van der Spoel, whether you would be in favour of a decision not to hear any plea by the defendant today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's unfortunately -- the defendant didn't have time to discuss the matters with his chosen counsel. However, I think the Rule 62 doesn't really allow for delaying the plea any further because I think it's very firm about the 30 days from the initial appearance, and that's actually today. And therefore, I think the best cause that I would suggest would be that you, Your Honour, declare a not guilty plea on behalf of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, Rule 62 is one rule, but Rule 127 -- would Rule 127 not apply in relation to Rule 62, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it may apply, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, Rule 62 might not be that cogent for me to enter a plea on behalf of the accused if he does not enter a plea. By the way, he said that if he's -- has to enter a plea, he will enter a plea of not guilty, which would give the same result. But we then agree that under Rule 62, together with Rule 127, I'm not -- I don't have to force the accused to enter a plea today; and if he doesn't, to enter a plea on his behalf, which would be a not guilty plea.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Van der Spoel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: I think your observations are quite correct concerning Rule 127 and 62. And a good cause, of course, is something that you can't blame my client for. He always wanted assigned counsel, and due to the proceedings, he hasn't been able to communicate with the chosen counsel, and he is very clear in his -- in his view that he does not want me to advise him. I've tried on several occasions, tried to discuss the indictment with me. But quite frankly -- and he said: Yes, but you won't defend me in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Perhaps you could defend me here but not there. That's one of the reasons he wants a lawyer not only to defend him here at the ICTY in The Hague, but also if his case will be referred to Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I think that your proposition is a very good one, that you delay the decision until my client has been able to discuss his situation and the indictment with his assigned counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This of course, Mr. Van der Spoel, is almost an implicit not guilty plea because I do not remember that once in this Tribunal a case was referred after an accused had entered a guilty plea. Usually sentencing is dealt with by this Tribunal. So therefore, it's -- from everything I hear at this moment it is a likelihood that there will be a not guilty plea entered, both from what you say and from what Mr. Zelenovic tells us. So therefore, from a practical point of view it might not make that much of a difference, apart from disclosure perhaps. Disclosure has not been done yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, disclosure has been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has been done.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: To the accused himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Today to the accused himself?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, actually yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday. Last time I made a mistake on the 13th of June about duty counsel, et cetera, what was still under discussion with the Association of Defence Counsel. I remembered the discussions. I'd forgotten that it had not resulted in any change of the Rules and it still has not resulted in any change of the Rules. That would also mean that the time-limit for preliminary motions would then start as from today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That also means that Mr. Ognjanovic, if he will be assigned counsel, if he takes over responsibilities from you, Mr. Van der Spoel, he should be informed that since disclosure has taken place today that he should keep in mind the time-limits set for any preliminary motions under the Rules. May I take it that you'll communicate with Mr. Ognjanovic about this matter? I do understand that he's passing a language test, which at least gives us a fair expectation that you'll be able to communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can promise you I will phone with OLAD and see if they can communicate with the chosen counsel. If not, I will communicate myself with the chosen counsel to explain these proceedings and, indeed, that yesterday the disclosure has taken place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zelenovic, the fact that your counsel of choice has not, either directly or indirectly, discussed with you the indictment, has not advised you and has not gone with you through all the elements of the indictment advising you on whether to enter a guilty plea or a not guilty plea is of great concern to the Trial Chamber. You had 30 days, and counsel, who was not qualified yet, could have taken steps in order to avoid further days. He should have been aware of the time-limits set by Chamber, time-limit under Rule 62; he also should have been aware and should have contacted Mr. Van der Spoel if he wanted a variation of the time-limits under Rule 127, because Rule 127 asks for a motion and good cause being shown. So it's of great concern to this Chamber that the counsel of preference has not, in anticipation of any assignment, has done what he should have done. The Registry is invited to send this portion of the transcript to Ognjanovic once he is assigned, and Mr. Van der Spoel is invited to ensure that Mr. Ognjanovic is aware of this criticism I'm expressing at this moment. Of course we could, at this moment, choose the very formal route that I would tell you that you have to enter a plea, or if you would not do so that I would enter a plea on your behalf. I prefer to hear a plea entered after you have had an opportunity to discuss matters with your counsel of preference. Therefore, although Rule 127 requires a motion, I consider it in the interests of justice that you'll be given another opportunity to enter a plea. I will look after it that the hearing on which I'll hear that plea will be scheduled immediately after the recess, independent on whether your counsel has made any arrangements for his holidays. I do not want to wait one minute more. Of course, preferably, we would have scheduled another plea hearing tomorrow. I will even look at it whether it's possible, but until now we did our utmost best to have another hearing tomorrow, but for scheduling reasons it was impossible. I would even explore an opportunity to have a very early hearing, perhaps at 8.00 or 8.30, so that we will not suffer any further delays. But until now it turned out to be practically impossible, but I'll give it another effort. So therefore, additional time will be given to you to discuss a plea with counsel of preference. Counsel of preference should communicate with Mr. Van der Spoel because I do not expect him to be assigned before tomorrow, although you never know, but I do not expect him to be assigned. Therefore, he should communicate with Mr. Van der Spoel after the meeting you have later today what the advice is. Mr. Van der Spoel is invited to actively initiate such communication. At the earliest possibility, we'll schedule a hearing, if possible tomorrow, but if not immediately after the recess, the recess that ends on the 7th of -- the recess that ends the weekend before the 7th of August. Mr. Zelenovic, have you understood my decision, that is to give you further time, either until tomorrow or certainly not later than immediately after the recess?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I can enter a plea tomorrow. He told me it would take us three hours to discuss things, and after that you will be able to enter a plea. In other words, I'm sure that I can enter a plea tomorrow. He should be here at noon talking to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, counsel should have been aware that this is the last of the 30 days, I think. Counsel should have been aware that if he arrives only midday that he might be late, and the Trial Chamber did its utmost best to schedule for tomorrow but we had practical problems. I mean, we've got three courtrooms, they're occupied the whole of the day by different Chambers. So therefore, counsel should be aware that it's the Court that schedules the hearings and not counsel. But I do understand that you're willing to cooperate and to enter a plea tomorrow if we can find a courtroom. Then is there anything else related to your detention situation or to your health which you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, everything is normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn and the parties should remain stand-by to receive information on when a new hearing will take place, either tomorrow or immediately after the recess. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.53 a.m.
